Commentary of Ibn 'Atiyya (al-Muharrar al-Wajiz) on surah 102, verses 1–8:

(p-680) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Tafsir of Surat al-Takathur

It is Meccan; I know of no disagreement about this.

The Exalted and Majestic said:

﴿Rivalry in worldly increase diverts you﴾ ﴿until you visit the graves﴾ ﴿No! You are going to know﴾ ﴿Again, no! You are going to know﴾ ﴿No! If only you knew with certainty of certainty﴾ ﴿You will surely see the Hellfire﴾ ﴿Again, you will surely see it with the eye of certainty﴾ ﴿Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the pleasure you enjoyed﴾

"Alhākum" (diverted you, distracted you) means: it occupied you with its pleasures. From it comes "idle talk and singing" (lahw al-hadith wal-aswat), and "diversion with women." This is a statement containing reproach, rebuke and regret. Ibn 'Abbas, Abu 'Imran al-Jawni and Abu Salih read "Ālhākum" as an interrogative.

"Takathur" is boasting about wealth, children and numbers in general. This is the habitual state of the people of this world and its sons, Arabs and others. Only the pious scholars escape it. al-A'sha said:

"I am not among the most numerous of them in pebbles, but glory belongs only to the one who multiplies."

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The son of Adam says: 'My wealth, my wealth.' Is there for you of your wealth anything except what you have eaten and used up, or worn and worn out, or given in charity and sent ahead?"

(p-681) The commentators differed concerning the meaning of His words: ﴿until you visit the graves﴾. Some of them said: until you mention the dead in your boasting about fathers and forebears, and you increase yourselves by the crumbling bones. Others said: the meaning is: until you die and visit your graves with your bodies, that is, you cut off your lives through multiplying. On this interpretation it is reported that a Bedouin heard this verse and said: "By the Lord of the Ka'ba, the people have been raised for the Resurrection, for the visitor departs and does not stay." al-Naqqash related this sentiment from 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz. Others said: this is a reproach for excessive visiting of graves; that is, you made your preoccupations which cut you off from knowledge and learning the visiting of graves, multiplying yourselves by those who preceded you and proclaiming their remembrance. And he said: Then the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I had forbidden you to visit graves; so visit them, and do not say what is abhorrent." So his prohibition was in the sense of the verse; then he permitted it afterward for the sake of admonition, not for the sake of boasting and vainglory, as people do in constant attendance upon them, decorating them with marble and stone, coloring them extravagantly, and building domes over them.

His words: ﴿No! You are going to know﴾ are a rebuke and a threat. Then He repeated "No!" for emphasis. People take from these two repeated rebukes and threats each according to his share of plunging into what he dislikes. This is the interpretation of the majority of people. 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "No! You will know in the graves; no! You will know at the Resurrection." al-Dahhak said: the first rebuke's threat is for the disbelievers, and the second for the believers. Malik ibn Dinar read "Kalla sayaʿlamun" in both places.

His words: ﴿No! If only you knew﴾: the answer to "law" (if) is omitted and understood from the context, that is, (p-682) you would have been restrained and hastened to save yourselves from destruction. "Al-yaqin" is the highest rank of knowledge. Then Allah informed people that they will see the Hellfire. Ibn 'Abbas and al-Kisa'i read "Latarūna" with a dammed ta', while the rest read it with a fatha, and this is the more preferred; likewise in the second. 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, read the first with a fatha and the second with a damma. Its damma is reported from Ibn Kathir and 'Asim.

"Taraunā" originally was *tarʾayūna*; the movement of the hamza was transferred to the ra', the ya' was changed to an alif because of its movement after a fathed letter, then the alif was deleted due to its being sukun and the sukun of the waw after it, then the heavy nun was added, so the waw was moved with a damma because of its sukun and the sukun of the first of the heavy nun, since the nun of i'rab was deleted for construction (binā'). Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: this is an address to the polytheists, and the meaning according to this is that it is the sight of its entering, which is the eye of certainty. Others said: the address is to all people, so it is like His words: ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it﴾ [Maryam: 71]; the meaning is that all will see it, and the saved will pass through, while the disbeliever will be hurled into it. His words: ﴿Again, you will surely see it with the eye of certainty﴾ are an emphasis of the report, and "ʿayn al-yaqin" is its reality and its ultimate degree. It is related from al-Hasan and Abu 'Amr that they made a hamza in "latarʾunna" and "latarʾunnahā," according to a variant from them. And it is related from Ibn Kathir: "Thumma latarūnnahā" with a damma on the ta'.

Then Allah informed that people will on that Day be questioned about their pleasures in the world: how they obtained them, and why they preferred them? In this there arise many questions according to each individual, from those who are led by one given understanding in the Book of Allah, the Exalted. Ibn Mas'ud, al-Sha'bi, Sufyan and Mujahid said: the pleasure is security and health. Ibn 'Abbas said: it is the body and the senses; a person is asked about how he used them. Ibn Jubayr said: it is everything one enjoys of food and drink. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ate dates, he and some of his companions, and they drank water over them, and he said to them: "This is from the pleasure about which you will be questioned." And one day the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), with Abu Bakr and 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, were hungry, and they went to the house of Abu al-Haytham ibn al-Tayhan, and he slaughtered a sheep for them, fed them bread and dates, and drew sweet water for them, and they were in shade. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, you will surely be questioned about the pleasure of this day." It is also reported from him (ﷺ) that he said: "The pleasure about which one is questioned is a morsel that sustains him, water that quenches him, and a garment that covers him." Abu Hurayra related from the Prophet (ﷺ) that "the pleasure about which one is questioned is cold water in summer." And the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever eats wheat bread and drinks cold water in shade, that is the pleasure about which he will be questioned." And the Prophet (ﷺ) said: (p-684) "A house that shelters you, a cloth that covers you, a morsel that steadies your heart, and whatever is beyond that is pleasure." And the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Every pleasure is one about which one will be questioned, except a pleasure spent in the way of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic."

The commentary of Surat [al-Takathur] is complete, and praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds.

And the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Every pleasure is one about which one will be questioned, except a pleasure spent in the way of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic."

The commentary of Surat [al-Takathur] is complete, and praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds.
